title: fix(errors): align three error names with their documented reference
body:
## Changes

- Three entries in `errors-data.ts` carry a `name` that doesn't match their export: `MissingLocale` → `MissingLocaleError`, `MissingIndexForInternationalization` → `MissingIndexForInternationalizationError`, `NoManifestAvailable` → `NoManifestAvailableError`. The other 129 all match.
- The error reference pages are published under the unsuffixed names, and the dev overlay prints `err.name` (`overlay.ts`, `this.text('#name', err.name)`). So a user hits the error, sees `MissingLocaleError`, and can't find it:

  | slug | status |
  | --- | --- |
  | `/en/reference/errors/missing-locale/` | 200 |
  | `/en/reference/errors/missing-locale-error/` | 404 |

  Same for the other two. The page for `missing-locale` never contains the string `MissingLocaleError`, so searching the docs for what the overlay showed finds nothing. That's the case the README's "users should always be able to find an error by searching" rule is there to prevent.
- Changed `name` to match the export in those three, plus a changeset.

Happy to flip this the other way if you'd rather keep the names and rename the exports — that would move the doc slugs to `missing-locale-error` etc. and break the existing URLs, which is why I went this direction, but it's your call.

## Testing

`packages/astro/test/units/manifest/ambient.test.ts` asserted `error.name === 'NoManifestAvailableError'`; updated to the new value. That's the only reference to any of the three strings in the repo.

I couldn't run the unit suite locally — it imports from `dist/`, and building needs the internal `astro-scripts` toolchain that my filtered install skipped, so I'm relying on CI for that. Biome is clean on both changed files.

## Docs

The reference pages are generated from this file, so they already show the unsuffixed names — this makes the runtime agree with them. No docs change needed as far as I can tell, but flagging in case you read it differently. /cc @withastro/maintainers-docs
